key_insight: A multi-protein serum/CSF signature can stratify ALS survival better than clinical factors and neurofilament alone, suggesting disease progression is reflected by multiple biological pathways.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this blood-based protein panel could help enrich ALS trials and improve prognostic counseling by identifying patients with different expected survival trajectories.
method: Longitudinal proteomics on 1,095 serum and CSF samples from 426 people with ALS
Age- and sex-adjusted Cox regression to find survival-associated proteins
Penalised Cox and joint modelling to build and test a prognostic protein panel
evidence_signal: The study linked 57 serum proteins and 5 CSF proteins to survival, and a 9-protein serum panel improved survival prediction versus models using clinical variables and NEFL.
watch_item: The signature still needs broader external validation and practical standardization before it can be used routinely in clinics or trials.
paper_title: A proteomic signature for prognostic stratification in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
